name: Complete Wing-Back 4-2-3-1

slots.why: Sweeper keeper is an extra passer in build-up and covers the space behind a higher line.
Complete wing-back (Attack) overlaps the playmaker on the left and gets in crosses and passes.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with passes into midfield.
Central defender who defends while his partner plays. Cover is the alternate.
Complete wing-back (Support) is the more cautious of the two, staying back more so one flank is safer.
Holding midfielder protects the back line and covers the flank when the wing-back goes forward.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the ball back, starts the counter-press and helps cover the wide areas.
Playmaker on the left drifts inside and creates from the half-space, which leaves the flank to the wing-back.
Advanced playmaker (Support) is the creative centre and links the flanks.
Inverted winger (Attack) cuts in from the right to shoot and attack the far post.
Deep-lying forward (Attack) links play but also runs at the defence, so the striker is not only a passer.

description: A 4-2-3-1 with two complete wing-backs who provide both the width and the creativity from the flanks, supported by playmakers inside them and a striker who drops to link play.
whyGood: Wing-backs who can cross, pass and dribble overload the flank against the opposition full-back, and the playmakers inside them give the team several ways to reach the box.
whyThisShape: Both flanks are overloaded: on the left the complete wing-back overlaps a playmaker who drifts inside, and on the right the wing-back supports an inside forward who cuts in. The double pivot stays behind them to cover the flanks when the wing-backs go forward, so the team attacks with width and stays protected.
whenToUse: When your two full-backs are among your best attacking players, or against a team that defends narrowly and leaves the flanks open.
whenNotToUse: Against quick wingers, if your wing-backs cannot recover; or when the double pivot cannot cover the flanks.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Keeps the ball in short passes among the wing-backs, playmakers and pivot.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: The sweeper keeper and ball-playing defender build from the back, so the wing-backs can advance.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Patient movement of the ball until the overlap or a pass from the half-space opens a chance.
instructionRationale.Overlap Left: The left wing-back overlaps the drifting playmaker to provide width.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Presses at once after losing the ball, to protect the space behind the wing-backs.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Presses higher up the pitch so the wing-backs are closer to the ball.

keyRequirements: Two complete wing-backs with stamina and skill
Playmakers on the left and in the middle
A double pivot to cover the flanks
